title: Key Features of Functions
objective: interpret key features of linear, quadratic, and absolute value functions given an equation or a graph
essential_question: How do key features help you understand functions and their graphs?
notes: Transcribed 2026-09-13 from the Savvas enVision Algebra 2 TE, Lesson 1-1 Practice & Problem Solving page (page footer reads "TOPIC 1 | 11 | LESSON 1"), Item Analysis table; source captures questionbank/calibration/sources/1-1_savvas_te_p11_full_page.png (sha256 deb6b0b007df505aea76310f8e8d466062a6011b896c82f79b6677523a53eb30) and questionbank/calibration/sources/1-1_savvas_te_p11_item_analysis_closeup.png (sha256 aa6ccb1ccfd554bfea173ace937cae943d041d4a62579e5e36a6757e1114b317). dok2_anchors: Practice #12 (Reason): given y = -1/2 x + 2 is negative on (4, inf) and positive on (-inf, 4), explain what happens on the graph at x = 4 -- interpret a sign change as a zero (Example 3 anchor).
dok3_anchors: Practice #13 (Error Analysis): describe and correct a student's positive/negative intervals for a graphed parabola, arguing why the zeros belong to neither interval (Example 3 anchor).

Practice #14-17 (Use Structure / Construct Arguments / Higher Order Thinking / Model With Mathematics): sketch a graph from a full set of key features; judge the claim that all linear functions are increasing or decreasing; define relative max/min and explain how to locate them; interpret increasing/decreasing speed graphs (Example 4 anchors).
Practice #28 (Communicate Precisely): describe and interpret every key feature of the sand-container graph from a rate and capacity (Example 4 anchor).
Practice #29, #33 (Make Sense and Persevere / Performance Task): read intercepts, sign intervals, and average rates of change off a real-context graph and explain what each means (Example 5 anchors).
Practice #30 (Model With Mathematics): write the battery-charge function, state domain and range with context, and solve for play time (Example 2 anchor).
